```{=html}
<script src="/apps/shared/mlt/recordings.js?v=2"></script>
<script src="/apps/shared/mlt/rec-catalogue.js?v=3"></script>
```

All the book CD tracks in one list. **Kind**, **tonality**, **meter** and **key** come from the track titles; where the title
says nothing, tonality and meter are read off the tune it is linked to and shown in *italics with a ?* until checked.
A recording is linked to a tune in the [tune collection](/practice/tunes.html) when their titles match; that tune's page then
lists the recording, and so does every MLT step that names the tune.

**Checking and filling in.** Pick *Show: needs checking*, change what is wrong, or press ✓ to confirm a row as it stands.
Edits stay in this browser until you press **Download recordings-meta.json**, put the file in `apps/shared/mlt/`, and run
`node scripts/mlt-recordings.mjs`. An empty tune box unlinks a wrong match.

**Timing maps.** 📱 opens [Mark Bars](/tools/mark-bars.html) for tapping bars and sections on a phone (kept in the phone's browser, sent by email at the end). ⏱ opens the recording in [Timestamp Notes](/tools/timestamp-notes.html): stamp the sections, tap the
downbeats, add chords if you like, then **Save** the song file as `apps/shared/mlt/timings/<recording id>.json` (the file name
it suggests) and rerun the script. ▦ opens the [Chord Grid by Ear](/practice/ear-grid.html) on the recording, using the timing map
when there is one.
